projects.name: Customer Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
End-to-end analytics dashboard delivering three data domains into one product surface:

1) CUSTOMER DATA (CSV): scheduled ingestion of customer CSV exports -> schema validation, cleaning/deduplication, PII masking, warehouse load.
2) APPLICATION LOGS: ingestion and parsing of application log files -> error-rate, latency and traffic metrics -> anomaly detection.
3) VISUALIZATION: reusable chart components, KPI tiles, time-series and log-explorer views composed into an interactive dashboard backed by a query API.

Structure: 5 milestones, each decomposed into leaf tasks with an execution complexity of 6 or below. Milestone records are roll-up containers, not single execution units.
Non-functional targets: WCAG AA accessibility, PII-safe by default, cost-guarded queries, observable pipelines.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-pipeline, csv-ingestion, log-analysis, visualization

tasks.name: M1 — Customer CSV Ingestion & Processing
tasks.details:
MILESTONE / ROLL-UP CONTAINER (never executed as one unit; work happens in its child tasks).

Goal: turn raw customer CSV exports into clean, typed, PII-safe, partitioned tables that the dashboard can query.

Exit criteria:
- A documented data contract for customer CSV files (columns, types, nullability, PII classification).
- Repeatable scheduled job that ingests new files, quarantines bad rows instead of failing the run, and is idempotent on re-run.
- Cleaning/dedup/normalization rules implemented and covered by tests.
- PII masked before data lands in any analytics-accessible table.
- Data quality checks run on every load and publish pass/fail metrics.
- Processed data written to partitioned warehouse tables with documented partitioning/clustering.

Complexity here reflects coordination across children, not a single task to execute. Sum of child estimates ≈ 78h.

tasks.name: M2 — Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details:
MILESTONE / ROLL-UP CONTAINER (executed through its child tasks).

Goal: make application log files queryable and turn them into reliability metrics (error rate, latency percentiles, traffic by endpoint) plus anomaly signals.

Exit criteria:
- Log source inventory: every log stream, its format, rotation/retention, and owner documented.
- Ingestion covers both live tail and backfill of historical files.
- Parser extracts structured fields (timestamp, level, service, endpoint, status, duration, trace id).
- Pre-aggregated metrics tables power the dashboard without full-scan queries.
- Anomaly detection flags error-rate and latency spikes with a documented, tunable threshold.
- Retention/sampling policy agreed and implemented so log storage cost stays bounded.

Complexity reflects coordination across children. Sum of child estimates ≈ 84h.

tasks.name: M3 — Dashboard Query API & Access Layer
tasks.details:
MILESTONE / ROLL-UP CONTAINER (executed through its child tasks).

Goal: a stable, secured query API that the dashboard frontend calls, so the UI never talks to the warehouse directly.

Exit criteria:
- Versioned API contract documented (endpoints, params, pagination, error model, sample payloads).
- Query service reads from the processed customer and log metric tables with a documented cache strategy.
- Authentication + authorization enforced, including row-level scoping so a user only sees permitted customer data.
- Rate limiting and per-query cost guards (max scanned bytes / timeout) in place.

Sum of child estimates ≈ 50h.

tasks.name: M4 — Visualization Components & Dashboard UI
tasks.details:
MILESTONE / ROLL-UP CONTAINER (executed through its child tasks).

Goal: ship the actual dashboard: a KPI summary row, time-series exploration, a customer cohort/funnel view, and a searchable log explorer — built from reusable components.

Exit criteria:
- KPI catalog with agreed definitions/formulas so numbers match across views.
- Reusable chart primitives documented in a lightweight component inventory.
- Each view implemented against the real query API (no mock-only components left behind).
- WCAG AA: keyboard reachable controls, text alternatives/data tables for charts, sufficient contrast.
- Acceptable render performance with realistic data volumes.

Sum of child estimates ≈ 120h.

tasks.name: M5 — QA, Deployment & Operations
tasks.details:
MILESTONE / ROLL-UP CONTAINER (executed through its child tasks).

Goal: make the whole stack testable, deployable and operable by someone other than its author.

Exit criteria:
- Deterministic fixture datasets (small CSV + sample logs) available for tests.
- Unit coverage on transforms/parsers, integration coverage across ingest -> load -> API.
- CI runs lint + tests; CD deploys to staging on merge and to prod behind an approval gate.
- Pipeline health dashboards + alerts (freshness, failure, row-count drift).
- Runbook: how to re-run a failed load, backfill a date range, rotate credentials, roll back.

Sum of child estimates ≈ 72h.

tasks.name: M1.1 Document customer CSV schema & data contract
tasks.details:
Inventory 3-5 representative customer CSV exports and write a single data contract doc.

Include per column: name, inferred type, nullable?, max length, allowed value set/enum, example value, source system owner.
Also classify every column as PII / sensitive / non-sensitive, and note known quirks (mixed date formats, locale decimal separators, trailing summary rows, duplicate header rows, inconsistent casing of country/state).

Deliverable: data-contract.md + a machine-readable schema file (JSON/YAML) that the validator and ingestion job both import.
Done when: schema file is committed, reviewed by whoever owns the customer export, and the validator consumes it.

tasks.name: M1.2 Build CSV ingestion job (discovery, decode, quarantine)
tasks.details:
Implement the ingestion entry point for customer CSV files.

Scope:
- Discover new/updated files in the landing location (or from a manifest) and record processed files so a re-run is idempotent (checksum + filename ledger).
- Stream-read the file rather than loading it fully into memory.
- Handle encoding detection (UTF-8 with/without BOM, common legacy encodings) and delimiter/quote/escape variance.
- Validate each row against the schema from M1.1; route invalid rows to a quarantine table with the reason and raw line, and continue the run.
- Emit run metrics: rows read, rows accepted, rows quarantined, duration.

Deliverable: ingestion module + CLI/job entry point + unit tests for encoding, malformed rows and idempotent re-run.
Done when: pointing it at the fixture files produces the same accepted/quarantined counts on two consecutive runs.

tasks.name: M1.3 Implement cleaning, dedup & normalization transforms
tasks.details:
Pure, unit-testable transforms applied after schema validation.

Scope:
- Trim/collapse whitespace, normalize unicode, fix casing conventions.
- Parse dates into ISO-8601 UTC, with the mixed-format rules captured in M1.1; reject rather than guess when ambiguous.
- Coerce numerics/currency with locale handling; record what was coerced.
- Normalize country/state to ISO codes, emails to lowercase (hash happens in M1.4).
- Deduplicate: define the business key (e.g. customer_id) and a survivorship rule for conflicting duplicate rows (most recent updated_at wins, tie-break by source priority).
- Attach lineage columns: source_file, ingested_at, row_hash.

Deliverable: transforms package with one test per rule, including a duplicate-conflict case.
Done when: a fixture set containing duplicates, bad dates and mixed casing yields the expected canonical output.

tasks.name: M1.4 Enforce PII masking & retention rules
tasks.details:
Make analytics-accessible customer data PII-safe by construction.

Scope:
- Using the PII classification from M1.1, define handling per field: drop, hash (salted, non-reversible), tokenize, or partial mask (e.g. j***@domain).
- Apply masking BEFORE the load step so raw values never reach analytics tables; raw landing zone keeps original files with restricted access and a documented TTL.
- Add a guard test that fails the build if a known PII column name appears unmasked in an analytics table schema.
- Document retention: how long raw files are kept, how deletion requests propagate to processed tables.

Deliverable: masking module + policy doc + guard test.
Done when: the guard test proves no unmasked PII column can reach the analytics schema, and a sample deletion request is traceable end-to-end.

tasks.name: M1.5 Build data quality validation suite
tasks.details:
Post-load checks that run on every load and publish results as metrics.

Checks to implement:
- Schema drift: expected columns/types vs actual.
- Volumetrics: row count within +/- X% of trailing 7-day average.
- Uniqueness of business key; null rate per critical column under threshold.
- Freshness: max(ingested_at) within SLA window.
- Referential sanity for any lookup/enum columns.

Behaviour: critical failures block promotion of the partition and alert; warnings are recorded only.
Deliverable: checks config (declarative) + runner + results table.
Done when: deliberately corrupted fixture data triggers each check exactly once with a clear message.

tasks.name: M1.6 Load processed data into partitioned warehouse tables
tasks.details:
Write the cleaned, masked dataset to its analytics home.

Scope:
- Define target table DDL (customer_current + partitioned history), types aligned to M1.1.
- Choose partitioning (by ingest date) and clustering keys based on the dashboard's actual filter patterns (M4.1 will confirm; use customer_id + segment as a starting assumption).
- Load strategy: atomic partition swap or MERGE on business key so readers never see partial data.
- Add table/column descriptions and a small data dictionary.

Deliverable: DDL scripts (versioned) + load step + a query that shows partition pruning is effective on a typical dashboard filter.
Done when: a load creates one new partition, existing partitions are untouched, and a date-filtered sample query scans only the target partition.

tasks.name: M2.1 Inventory log sources & define log format spec
tasks.details:
Short discovery task so parsing work is not guesswork.

Produce a table of every application log stream: service name, file path / stream, format (JSON lines, plaintext, syslog, framework default), rotation & retention, volume per day, timezone of timestamps, and owning team.

Then capture 20-30 real sample lines per format (redacted of secrets/tokens) and write a format spec: field name, type, nullability, example, extraction approach (native JSON field vs regex named group).

Deliverable: log-sources.md + sample fixture file per format.
Done when: each format has at least one sample and every field the dashboard needs is mapped to a source field.

tasks.name: M2.2 Build log ingestion job with historical backfill
tasks.details:
Move log files/lines into the store the pipeline reads from.

Scope:
- Two modes: (a) incremental tail of new lines from the current offset (b) backfill over a date range of archived files.
- Track per-source offsets/watermarks so restarts neither duplicate nor skip records; write partition-by-hour so late-arriving lines are handled.
- Compress on write and drop obvious noise (health-check spam) at ingest with a documented filter list.
- Backpressure: cap ingest rate so a large backfill does not starve the live path.

Deliverable: ingest job with both modes + checkpoint store + tests for restart-mid-file and duplicate delivery.
Done when: killing the job mid-file and restarting produces no lost lines and no duplicates on the backfill range.

tasks.name: M2.3 Implement log parser & field extraction
tasks.details:
Turn raw log lines into a typed record per the M2.1 format spec.

Scope:
- Per-format parsers (JSON lines passthrough, regex/Grok for plaintext) emitting a common record: timestamp (UTC), level, service, host, endpoint/route, status_code, duration_ms, trace_id, message, raw.
- Multi-line stack traces grouped with their parent error line.
- Unparseable lines go to a parse-failure sample table with a counter, never silently dropped.
- Track parse success rate per source as a metric.

Deliverable: parser modules + per-format unit tests (happy path, malformed line, multiline stack trace, timezone edge case).
Done when: fixture samples from every source parse at >=99% success and a deliberately broken line is counted, not lost.

tasks.name: M2.4 Build pre-aggregated reliability metrics tables
tasks.details:
Pre-compute the numbers the dashboard renders, at 1-minute and 1-hour granularity.

Metrics per service + endpoint + status class:
- Request count, error count, error rate (5xx, 4xx separately).
- Latency percentiles p50/p95/p99 from duration_ms (document the percentile method - exact vs t-digest - and its error bound).
- Unique trace count, top error messages (normalized, top 20).

Implementation: incremental rollup job over hourly partitions, idempotent per (date, hour, service) so a re-run overwrites cleanly.
Deliverable: rollup job + DDL + a validation query comparing rollup counts to raw counts for a sample day (<0.5% drift).
Done when: dashboard-typical queries hit only the rollup tables and return in under 2s on realistic volume.

tasks.name: M2.5 Add anomaly detection for error-rate & latency spikes
tasks.details:
Flag deviations worth a human look, without drowning the team in noise.

Scope:
- Baseline per service/endpoint using a rolling 7-day same-weekday-hour profile (seasonality-aware).
- Detect: error-rate above baseline + N sigma, p95 latency above baseline, and sudden zero-traffic (service down signal).
- Severity levels + minimum-duration guard (e.g. must hold 5 minutes) to suppress single-minute blips.
- Output to an anomalies table: window, metric, observed vs expected, severity, contributing dimensions.
- Tunable thresholds in config, not code.

Deliverable: detector job + backtest report over 30 days of history showing flagged windows and a rough false-positive rate.
Done when: backtest correctly flags at least one known past incident and the FP rate is judged acceptable by the team.

tasks.name: M2.6 Implement log retention, sampling & cost controls
tasks.details:
Keep storage growth predictable.

Scope:
- Tiering: hot (7-14 days, full detail), warm (90 days, rollups only), cold/archive (raw compressed, restore on request).
- Sampling policy for very high-volume debug-level lines (keep all WARN/ERROR; sample INFO/DEBUG at a documented rate with trace_id-aware keeping).
- Enforce retention with a scheduled cleanup job and a dry-run mode.
- Publish storage bytes by tier and by service so cost is visible.

Deliverable: retention config + cleanup job + cost visibility query.
Done when: dry-run over current data shows exactly which partitions would expire, and no query in the dashboard reads data older than the hot/warm boundaries without falling back to archive.

tasks.name: M3.1 Define query API contract & error model
tasks.details:
Specify the interface before building it, driven by the views the dashboard needs.

Endpoints to specify (read-only): KPIs summary, customer segment breakdown, customer cohort/funnel, log time-series (metric + interval + filters), log explorer search, anomaly list.

For each: query params (date range, interval, segment, service, endpoint, severity, pagination cursor), response shape with units and nullability, max ranges allowed, and a consistent error envelope (code, message, details, request_id).

Deliverable: OpenAPI spec (or equivalent) + example payloads + a shared generated client/types for the frontend.
Done when: frontend and backend agree on the spec and a mock server serving the examples unblocks M4 work.

tasks.name: M3.2 Implement query service with caching
tasks.details:
Implement the read path behind the API contract, using the M1.6 customer tables and M2.4 rollups.

Scope:
- Parameterized queries only (no string-built SQL); one handler per endpoint in M3.1.
- Always push date-range filters into the partition key so queries prune.
- Cache: short-TTL (30-60s) response cache keyed by normalized query, plus a longer TTL for historic (closed) periods; explicit invalidation hook when a new partition loads.
- Structured logging of query duration, rows scanned, cache hit/miss.

Deliverable: service + integration tests against fixture warehouse + a simple load test (e.g. 20 rps for 5 minutes).
Done when: p95 latency is under target at the expected concurrency and repeated identical requests hit the cache.

tasks.name: M3.3 Implement authentication & row-level authorization
tasks.details:
Ensure a viewer only sees customer data they are entitled to.

Scope:
- Integrate with the existing identity provider (session/token validation, no bespoke password store).
- Role model: viewer (aggregates only), analyst (row-level detail within their region/segment), admin.
- Enforce row-level scoping in the query layer (mandatory filter injection), not in the UI.
- Deny-by-default tests: a viewer requesting detail rows gets 403; an analyst scoped to region A cannot retrieve region B rows even with a hand-crafted request.

Deliverable: auth middleware + policy definitions + authorization test suite.
Done when: the negative tests pass and no endpoint returns unscoped customer rows.

tasks.name: M3.4 Add rate limiting & query cost guards
tasks.details:
Protect the warehouse from expensive or abusive requests.

Scope:
- Per-user and per-IP rate limits with sensible burst allowance; 429 with Retry-After.
- Cost guards: hard max date range per endpoint, max rows/pages, statement timeout, and a scan-bytes ceiling that rejects rather than runs.
- Anomalous-usage logging (one user issuing many heavy queries) with an alert.
- Config-driven limits so they can be tuned without a deploy.

Deliverable: middleware/config + tests that a too-wide range and a too-large page are rejected with clear errors.
Done when: guard tests pass and a documented "cost of a typical dashboard session" figure exists.

tasks.name: M4.1 Write KPI catalog & dashboard information architecture
tasks.details:
Agree what the dashboard answers before drawing charts.

Deliver:
- 8-12 KPIs with exact formula, grain, source table/column, filters applied, and known caveats. Example: Active customers (30d), New customers, Churn-risk count, Revenue per segment, Error rate (5xx %), p95 latency, Requests/min, Open anomalies.
- For each KPI: owner, target/threshold, and how it should be displayed (number + trend, sparkline, gauge).
- Page layout IA: which cards sit where, default date range, default filters, and the drill-down path from each KPI.

Deliverable: kpi-catalog.md + wireframe (low-fi is fine).
Done when: a stakeholder confirms the definitions and no two KPIs compute the same name differently.

tasks.name: M4.2 Build chart primitives & design tokens
tasks.details:
Foundation components every view reuses, so we build each chart once.

Scope:
- Tokens: color palette (categorical + sequential, contrast-checked), typography scale, spacing, elevation.
- Wrappers: <ChartFrame> (title, subtitle, loading, empty, error states, download CSV), <TimeSeriesChart>, <BarBreakdown>, <DataTable>, <TrendDelta>.
- Consistent number formatting (compact, thousands separators, %, ms) and timezone-aware axis labels.
- Loading/empty/error state built into each primitive so no view invents its own.

Deliverable: component library entries + a small storybook/gallery page rendering each with fixture data.
Done when: all primitives render in isolation with the four states (loading, empty, error, data) and pass contrast checks.

tasks.name: M4.3 Build KPI summary tiles
tasks.details:
The top row of the dashboard: at-a-glance numbers from the KPI catalog.

Scope:
- Tile rendering value + unit + delta vs previous period with direction-aware colouring (and an up/down arrow or sign, never colour alone).
- Each tile fetches from the KPIs endpoint; partial failure shows a per-tile error, not a blank page.
- Clicking a tile applies the corresponding filter/drill-down defined in M4.1.
- Covers the 8-12 KPIs from M4.1 — if more than 12, split into primary row + secondary row rather than shrinking text.

Deliverable: tile component + wiring to real API + tests for delta formatting and error isolation.
Done when: tiles show correct numbers against a hand-verified fixture and survive an endpoint failure gracefully.

tasks.name: M4.4 Build time-series exploration view
tasks.details:
The core charting surface for metrics over time.

Scope:
- Metric selector (error rate, request count, p50/p95/p99 latency), interval selector (1m/1h/1d) with automatic downsampling when the range is too wide, and date-range picker.
- Filters: service, endpoint, status class. Filters must be reflected in the URL so a view is shareable/bookmarkable.
- Tooltip with exact values + timestamp in the viewer's timezone; brush-to-zoom on the x-axis.
- Handle sparse/missing buckets explicitly (gap vs zero) and show a partial-data marker for the most recent incomplete interval.

Deliverable: view component + URL state handling + tests for interval auto-selection and missing buckets.
Done when: toggling filters produces shareable URLs and the chart renders correctly for 1h, 7d and 90d ranges.

tasks.name: M4.5 Build customer segment & cohort breakdown views
tasks.details:
The customer-data half of the dashboard, built on the M1.6 tables.

Scope:
- Segment breakdown: customers/revenue by segment, region, plan; sortable bar/table with % of total.
- Cohort view: signup-month cohorts with retention by period (month 0..N); render as a heatmap-style table with accessible text values.
- Funnel: signup -> activated -> active step counts with drop-off percentages (definition of each step taken from M4.1 and written on the card).
- Small-cohort suppression: cells below a threshold (e.g. n<10) are masked so individuals can't be inferred.

Deliverable: two views + tests for percentage math and small-cell suppression.
Done when: totals reconcile with a SQL cross-check and no cell below the suppression threshold is displayed.

tasks.name: M4.6 Build log explorer & error drill-down view
tasks.details:
Where someone investigating an incident actually works.

Scope:
- Faceted search over parsed logs: service, level, time range, endpoint, status, free-text query on message; result count shown before running heavy queries.
- Paginated/cursor results with virtualized rows (no thousands of DOM nodes).
- Row expansion shows full message + grouped stack trace + trace_id link-out.
- "Copy permalink" that reproduces the exact query and range.
- Guardrails: queries outside the retention window or too broad are rejected with a clear message and a one-click "narrow to last hour" suggestion.

Deliverable: explorer view + virtualized table + tests for query serialization and permalink round-trip.
Done when: a p95-loading search over 7 days of fixture logs stays responsive and permalinks restore identical results.

tasks.name: M4.7 Build anomaly panel & alert timeline
tasks.details:
Surface the M2.5 anomalies in the UI so they are actionable rather than a table nobody reads.

Scope:
- Timeline/list of anomalies: severity badge, metric, window, observed vs expected (e.g. "error rate 4.2% vs 0.3% expected"), affected service/endpoint.
- Each item expands to a pre-filtered link into the time-series view and log explorer for that window.
- Filter by severity and service; acknowledge/snooze an anomaly (state stored, not just local).
- Empty state that says "no anomalies in this range" with the detection windows listed, so silence is interpretable.

Deliverable: panel component + acknowledge API call + tests for severity sorting and empty state.
Done when: a seeded anomaly from the backtest appears with correct links and can be acknowledged.

tasks.name: M4.8 Compose dashboard page, layout & responsive behaviour
tasks.details:
Assemble the views into the actual page and make the global controls work.

Scope:
- Global filter bar (date range, segment, service) that all cards subscribe to, with a single source of truth in URL state.
- Grid layout per the M4.1 wireframe: KPI row, time-series, customer breakdown/cohort, log explorer, anomaly panel.
- Responsive breakpoints: cards stack, charts get minimum sensible height, tables scroll horizontally rather than crushing columns.
- Per-card loading skeletons and independent error boundaries so one slow endpoint does not blank the page.
- Save/restore a "view" preset (the filter combination) and a reset-to-defaults control.

Deliverable: composed page + filter bar + layout tests at 3 breakpoints (sm/md/lg).
Done when: changing a global filter updates every subscribed card, and a single failing card leaves the rest of the page usable.

tasks.name: M4.9 Run accessibility review & fix WCAG AA issues
tasks.details:
Make the dashboard usable with keyboard and screen reader.

Checklist to verify and fix:
- Every interactive control (range picker, metric selector, filters, table sort) reachable and operable by keyboard with visible focus.
- Charts have a text alternative: an adjacent collapsible data table and an aria-describedby summary ("error rate peaked 4.2% at 14:05").
- Colour is never the only signal (delta arrows, severity labels, patterns/shapes for categorical series).
- Contrast >= 4.5:1 for text, >= 3:1 for UI/graphical objects; verify palette from M4.2.
- Form labels, landmark regions, page title, and logical heading order; table headers properly scoped.

Deliverable: audit notes + fixes + automated axe check in CI with a documented allowlist (empty preferred).
Done when: keyboard-only walkthrough of every view completes without traps and axe reports no serious/critical issues.

tasks.name: M4.10 Tune frontend performance with realistic data volumes
tasks.details:
Make sure the dashboard is still usable beyond the demo dataset.

Scope:
- Define a realistic load profile (e.g. 500k customer rows, 30 days of logs at production rate) and a synthetic generator/fixture at that scale.
- Measure: initial load, time-to-interactive, chart render, explorer pagination latency.
- Fix the top offenders only (code-split heavy chart libs, paginate/virtualize, memoize transforms, debounce filters, downsample series client-side when >N points).
- Set a performance budget and record before/after numbers so regressions are visible.

Deliverable: perf report + budget config in CI + applied fixes.
Done when: each measured path meets the budget (or the exception is documented and accepted).

tasks.name: M5.1 Create deterministic test fixtures & seed data
tasks.details:
Shared fixtures everything else tests against, so results are reproducible.

Deliver:
- Customer CSVs: a clean small set (~50 rows), plus adversarial variants — duplicate customers with conflicting rows, bad dates, mixed encodings, missing required field, extra unknown column, empty file.
- Log fixtures: 20-30 lines per supported format, including a malformed line, a multi-line stack trace, and a timezone/DST boundary case.
- A synthetic generator for volume tests (parameterized row count / log rate) with a fixed seed.
- Fixtures live in the repo under a documented path; no PII — all values fake but realistically shaped.

Done when: `make fixtures` (or equivalent) regenerates byte-identical output and every test in M5.2/M5.3 consumes these instead of ad-hoc data.

tasks.name: M5.2 Unit tests for transforms & parsers
tasks.details:
Close the loop on the pure-logic layer (M1.3 transforms, M2.3 parsers, M1.4 masking).

Scope:
- One test per documented rule; table-driven where possible (input row -> expected output row).
- Masking tests assert the PII value cannot be recovered and that hashes are salted/stable per tenant.
- Parser tests cover each format's happy path plus the malformed/multiline/DST cases from M5.1.
- Assert on failure messages, not just pass/fail, so debugging is fast.

Target: >=80% line coverage on the transform/parser packages; coverage reported in CI but no blanket enforcement on UI code.
Done when: the suite runs in under 2 minutes locally and a deliberately introduced bug in a transform is caught.

tasks.name: M5.3 Write integration & end-to-end pipeline tests
tasks.details:
Prove the pieces work together, not just in isolation.

Scenarios (each with fixture input and asserted output):
1. CSV fixture -> ingest -> transform -> mask -> load -> API returns expected aggregates and zero unmasked PII.
2. Log fixture -> ingest -> parse -> rollup -> API returns expected error rate and p95.
3. Re-running any stage twice produces identical results (idempotency).
4. Bad-row path: invalid CSV rows are quarantined and the run still succeeds with correct counts.
5. Authz: viewer/analyst scoping enforced through the full stack.

Run against an ephemeral/local warehouse (containerized) so anyone can run it; seed via M5.1 fixtures.
Done when: all five scenarios pass in a clean checkout with one command.

tasks.name: M5.4 Set up CI pipeline (lint, typecheck, tests, build)
tasks.details:
A single required check that gates merges.

Pipeline stages, in order and fast-failing: format/lint -> typecheck -> unit tests -> integration tests (containerized warehouse) -> build artifacts -> accessibility check (axe) -> schema/PII guard test.

Scope:
- Cache dependencies; target under 10 minutes total.
- Upload test reports/coverage as artifacts; surface flaky tests explicitly rather than retrying silently.
- Branch protection: pipeline must pass before merge to main.

Done when: a PR with a deliberate lint error, a failing unit test and a PII-guard violation is blocked at the right stage with a clear message.

tasks.name: M5.5 Set up staging & production deployment with rollback
tasks.details:
Ship safely and reversibly.

Scope:
- Environments: staging (auto-deploy on merge to main, seeded with fixtures) and production (manual approval gate).
- Deploy units: warehouse DDL migrations, pipeline jobs (scheduled), query API, frontend. Each independently deployable; migrations run forward-only with a tested rollback or a documented compensating step.
- Smoke test post-deploy: hit key API endpoints, assert non-empty KPI response and no auth bypass.
- Rollback: one command/button to return to the previous version; document the data implications (do not roll back destructive migrations blindly).

Done when: a staged release can be deployed and rolled back to the prior version in staging with data intact, and the production approval gate is enforced.

tasks.name: M5.6 Add monitoring & alerting for pipelines and API
tasks.details:
Know when it breaks before a stakeholder tells you.

Scope:
- Metrics: job success/failure/duration per pipeline stage, rows/quarantined counts, freshness lag, API error rate + p95 latency, cache hit rate, query cost per day.
- Alerts (with runbook link in the alert body): pipeline failed, freshness SLA breached, data-quality critical failure, API error rate above threshold, cost anomaly.
- A small operations dashboard reusing the M4.2 primitives (dogfooding the components).
- Alert routing: one on-call channel; no silent-only-log alerts.

Done when: a forced pipeline failure and a forced freshness breach both page the on-call channel within the expected window, and each alert links to the relevant runbook section.

tasks.name: M5.7 Write runbook, docs & handover
tasks.details:
Make the system operable and understood by someone who did not build it.

Contents:
- Architecture diagram (sources -> landing -> transforms -> warehouse -> API -> UI) with the owner of each hop.
- How to: add a new CSV source, add a new log format, add a KPI and its chart, change a retention policy.
- Incident procedures: re-run a failed load, backfill a date range, restore from archive, revoke a user, roll back a release.
- Data dictionary + PII map pointer, plus known limitations and "what this dashboard does not measure".
- Handover session: walk through runbook with the receiving team and record gaps they find.

tasks.name: M1.3a Normalize & type-cast customer fields
tasks.details:
First half of the transform work: turn validated strings into correct, canonical values.

Scope:
- Whitespace/unicode cleanup and casing conventions (names, emails lowercased, country/state trimmed).
- Date parsing to ISO-8601 UTC using only the formats listed in M1.1; ambiguous values raise a typed error rather than guessing.
- Numeric/currency coercion with locale handling; emit a coercion record (field, raw value, parsed value) for audit.
- Country/state to ISO-3166 codes; unknown values pass through flagged, never silently dropped.

Deliverable: normalize module + table-driven tests per rule.
Done when: a fixture row with mixed casing, a European decimal comma and a DD/MM/YYYY date comes out canonical, and an ambiguous date is rejected with a clear message.
